answer: Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 2 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. Because the relic weights are read from the anchor ledger at case open, the summit audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. A farm must therefore post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. That is 4 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
